candidates.claim: `CompletelyRegularSpace.of_exists_uniformSpace` is declared under the section variable `variable [t : TopologicalSpace α] [CompletelyRegularSpace α]` (line 111), so the class becomes an *argument* of the theorem, and that argument is literally the conclusion: `#check @CompletelyRegularSpace.of_exists_uniformSpace` gives `∀ {α} [t : TopologicalSpace α] [CompletelyRegularSpace α], (∃ u, u.toTopologicalSpace = t) → CompletelyRegularSpace α`, which is provable by `inferInstance` without using `h` at all. So the content announced in the module docstring ("Uniformizable spaces are completely regular") is not what is proved. The same variable also makes the `mpr` half of `completelyRegularSpace_iff_exists_uniformSpace` (line 123) vacuous: it reads "assuming the space is completely regular, it is completely regular iff it is uniformizable". This is not the style of the area: the sibling `completelyRegularSpace_iff_isOpen` (Mathlib/Topology/Separation/CompletelyRegular.lean:72) and `completelyRegularSpace_iff_isInducing_stoneCechUnit` (ibid.:190) are stated with only `[TopologicalSpace X]` in scope.
candidates.requested_change:
Restrict the variable to line 111 to the topology, and give the one declaration that genuinely needs the hypothesis its own binder:

```lean
variable [t : TopologicalSpace α]

public theorem CompletelyRegularSpace.exists_uniformSpace [CompletelyRegularSpace α] :
    ∃ (u : UniformSpace α), u.toTopologicalSpace = t := ...

public theorem CompletelyRegularSpace.of_exists_uniformSpace
    (h : ∃ (u : UniformSpace α), u.toTopologicalSpace = t) :
    CompletelyRegularSpace α := by
  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := h
  infer_instance

public theorem completelyRegularSpace_iff_exists_uniformSpace :
    CompletelyRegularSpace α ↔ ∃ (u : UniformSpace α), u.toTopologicalSpace = t :=
  ⟨@CompletelyRegularSpace.exists_uniformSpace α t, CompletelyRegularSpace.of_exists_uniformSpace⟩
```
The `@`-application in the iff still elaborates (the instance argument is supplied by unification with the left-hand side of the `Iff`), and the proof of `of_exists_uniformSpace` still works because `u : UniformSpace α` introduced by `obtain` is used as an instance by `infer_instance`.
